questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down?

options.text: Turn on the right turn signal, then the left turn signal.
Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash the brake lights.
Swerve side to side to get other drivers' attention.
Turn all lights on and off several times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash the brake lights.
questions.explanation: Tap your brake pedal lightly a few times to make the brake lights flash. This warns drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand so you can eat or drink while driving.
With one hand at a time, switching between hands.
Loosely to allow your hands to move freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands. Place your hands on opposite sides of the wheel for better control.

questions.question: How might you recognize a distracted driver?

options.text: They drive at a steady speed.
They are looking at their cell phone.
They are not talking to passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are looking at their cell phone.
questions.explanation: A distracted driver may drift between lanes, drive at changing speeds, use a cell phone, look at a map, eat, or talk with passengers.

questions.question: What do many drivers do in bad weather?
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow closely behind trucks.
questions.explanation: In bad weather when visibility is poor, many drivers follow trucks closely. Keep a safe distance between your vehicle and the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: When should a school bus stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Between 15 and 50 feet before the nearest rail.
The bus does not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between 15 and 50 feet before the nearest rail.
questions.explanation: School buses must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail. This gives you a good view of the tracks. Look and listen for trains before crossing.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most heavy trucks have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Air brakes
questions.explanation: Most heavy trucks have dual air brake systems for safety.

questions.question: What should you do before driving a bus that has been parked for several days?

options.text: Assume the interior is fine and begin driving.
Walk through the bus to check for damage.
Ask passengers to check the interior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for damage.
questions.explanation: Before operating a parked bus, always check the interior to ensure everything is in safe working condition for passengers.

questions.question: How far behind your vehicle should you place warning devices when stopped on a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: 10, 100, and 200 feet
questions.explanation: Place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind your vehicle when stopped on a highway.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, what must you NOT do regarding oil?

options.text: Show where the dipstick is located.
Show that the oil level is safe.
Show that the oil level is above the refill mark.
Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: You must show where the dipstick is, that the oil level is safe, and that it is above the refill mark. The oil level should never be below the refill mark.

questions.question: If hydraulic brakes fail, how can you slow down your vehicle?

options.text: Let the truck run out of gas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear.
questions.explanation: If your hydraulic brakes fail, shift into a lower gear to help slow down your vehicle.

questions.question: If you must drive a school bus during high winds, what should you do?

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when driving a school bus in high winds. Hold the steering wheel firmly and watch for wind gusts.

questions.question: When backing a vehicle into an alley, what should you do first?

options.text: Pull directly into the alley parking space.
Turn your vehicle to the right to position yourself in front of the alley.
Pull past the alley and stop at a right angle to the outer boundary.
Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary.
questions.explanation: First, pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking space.

questions.question: Before driving a bus that has been left unattended, what should you do?

options.text: Look for animals that may have gotten on board.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the interior for damage.
questions.explanation: People may damage unattended buses. Walk through the bus and check the interior for any damage before driving.

questions.question: If fog covers the road, what is the best thing to do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving.
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is dangerous. If possible, do not drive in foggy conditions.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep does an adult need each day to stay alert?
questions.correctAnswerText: Seven to eight hours
questions.explanation: Most people need seven to eight hours of sleep each night to stay alert and drive safely.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should a driver do?

options.text: Cross before a train reaches the crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce speed.
questions.explanation: Always expect a train at every crossing. Do not rely on signals or sound to tell you if a train is coming. Slow down at every crossing and never try to beat a train.

questions.question: If a bus leans toward the outside of a banked curve, what does this mean?

options.text: The bus is being driven too slow.
The bus is being driven at the right speed.
The bus is being driven too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bus is being driven too fast.
questions.explanation: A bus leaning toward the outside of a curve means it is going too fast. Slow down when entering a curve.

questions.question: Is it good to look far ahead while driving?

options.text: No, because you cannot do anything about hazards far away.
Yes, to spot hazards early and have time to respond.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, to spot hazards early and have time to respond.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This lets you see hazards early and have time to respond safely.

questions.question: If the ABS warning light comes on while driving, what does it mean?

options.text: The ABS has just been activated.
The ABS is not working properly.
The ABS needs to be activated.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: A yellow ABS light warns the driver that something is wrong with the braking system. You may have lost ABS on one or more wheels.

questions.question: When using a turn signal, what should you avoid doing?

options.text: Cancel the turn signal after the turn.
Leave the turn signal on long after the turn is complete.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the turn signal on long after the turn is complete.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep signaling until the turn or lane change is done. Then cancel the signal so you do not confuse other drivers.
